findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Pin the Python `<<-` dedent helper against Terraform's actual algorithm (e.g. assert the helper reproduces the known 1021-char/1025-byte value for docker_buildkit_cache_high AND at least one description with non-uniform indentation), so the guard's byte count provably matches what the provider validates.
evidence: "applies the same `<<-` dedent the Terraform parser applies"
AC5 only proves the ONE fixed description reaches a plan; it does not size the other 33
AC4 anchors only the docker_buildkit_cache_high value, not the general dedent fidelity
findings.finding: AC3's guard reimplements Terraform's `<<-` heredoc dedent in Python, but the plan never pins that reimplementation against Terraform's actual dedent algorithm (strip the leading whitespace common to all lines). If the Python dedent diverges from the provider's, the guard's byte count differs from what the provider validates, giving false confidence for the 33 descriptions that `terraform plan` (AC5) does not independently size.
scenarios: A future description uses mixed indentation that Terraform dedents differently than the Python helper, so the guard passes at 1024 bytes while the provider rejects it at 1025

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State how the in-Python `<<-` dedent used by the guard test is validated to match Terraform's actual rendering (e.g. anchor one known description's Python-measured byte count against a value observed from real terraform output), so the guard cannot diverge from the provider's own length check.
evidence: "applies the same `<<-` dedent the Terraform parser applies, and asserts the rendered value is at most 1024 UTF-8 BYTES"
AC5 runs real terraform plan but is a manual capture, not a recurring assertion
The Python re-implementation of dedent is a substitute for the provider's own length check
findings.finding: The recurring guard test re-implements Terraform's `<<-` heredoc dedent and description extraction in Python; if that in-Python parser diverges from the AWS provider's actual byte-length computation (e.g. different dedent rules, trailing-newline handling, or which attribute counts), the test can go green while `terraform plan` still fails on bytes — the substitute parser is a proxy for the real provider validation. AC5 exercises real `terraform plan` but only as a one-time manual check, not as part of the recurring suite.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a note or sub-assertion that pins the Python dedent against a Terraform-observed byte count for at least the docker_buildkit_cache_high description (1021 post-fix, 1025 pre-fix), documenting that the two measurements agree.

findings.finding: The plan's premise 'Nothing in the repository currently measures these' and 'test_alarm_actions_terraform.py ... assert on alarm actions and windows, not on description size in any unit' is false: test_alarm_actions_terraform.py already contains test_alarm_descriptions_fit_the_aws_limit which renders every heredoc/quoted alarm_description (with the same <<- dedent) and asserts len(rendered) <= 1024 — it measures description size today, in CHARACTERS. This is the exact units defect the plan diagnoses, so the pre-existing guard is the natural fix site.
findings.location: Evidence section ('Nothing in the repository currently measures these...') and Approach step 2 / AC3 / AC4
scenarios: A new byte-measuring test is added while the existing char-measuring test_alarm_descriptions_fit_the_aws_limit is left in place, producing two overlapping guards asserting different units.
The existing character-based guard continues to pass the malformed 1021-char/1025-byte description, so it never protected the drift lane and a reader trusts a guard that measures the wrong unit.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the existing test_alarm_descriptions_fit_the_aws_limit to measure len(rendered.encode('utf-8')) against 1024 bytes (updating its docstring/comment that say 'character' limit), rather than adding a parallel test; or explicitly justify a second test and delete/retarget the char-based one.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Broaden the AC3 guard to measure ALL alarm_description values (both heredoc and quoted single-line strings), since the 1024-byte provider limit applies to both and quoted over-limit descriptions would re-blind the drift lane identically.
evidence: AC3: 'asserts that EVERY heredoc alarm_description across every infra/terraform/*.tf file renders to at most 1024 UTF-8 bytes'
search shows quoted assignments: infra/terraform/monitoring.tf:288 and :363, monitoring_4b6e.tf:14/42/70/94, monitoring.tf:155/181/210
monitoring.tf:363 quoted description contains an em dash: 'not here — see infra/runbooks/...' — the exact risky construct the plan flags, but outside the guard's scope
The named problem is that ANY over-limit alarm_description fails `terraform plan` for the whole account, not just heredoc ones
findings.finding: The preventive guard (AC3) measures only HEREDOC alarm_description values, but the AWS provider's 1024-byte limit applies equally to QUOTED (single-line string) alarm_description assignments, several of which exist in the repo (e.g. monitoring.tf lines 288/363, monitoring_4b6e.tf) and one of which already contains an em dash. A future over-limit quoted description would re-blind the entire drift lane in the same way as the current defect, and the proposed test would not catch it.
scenarios: A future operator authors or extends a quoted single-line alarm_description past 1024 bytes; the guard passes but `terraform plan` fails and the drift lane goes blind again
An em dash is added to an already-near-limit quoted description
findings.suggested_fix: Have the parser capture both `alarm_description = <<-EOT ... EOT` heredocs and `alarm_description = "..."` quoted forms, apply dedent only to the heredoc case, and assert <=1024 UTF-8 bytes on every captured value; adjust the discovery-count assertion to reflect the larger total.

findings.finding: The plan proposes a NEW parallel pytest module for a guard that already exists, and mischaracterizes the existing guard's coverage. `tests/unit/test_alarm_actions_terraform.py::test_alarm_descriptions_fit_the_aws_limit` already parses every heredoc and quoted `alarm_description`, applies the same `<<-` dedent, enforces a size limit, and has an anti-vacuity floor — its only defect is that it measures CHARACTERS not BYTES, which is precisely the units bug this plan diagnoses.
findings.location: Evidence section ('assert on alarm actions and windows, not on description size in any unit') and AC3 ('A new pytest test ... A new test module under tests/unit/')
scenarios: A future contributor maintains both the old character-based guard and the new byte-based module, which disagree on the same invariant.
The new module's discovery-count floor (≥34) drifts from the existing floor (18 heredoc + 3 quoted), so a reformat silences one guard while the other stays green.
Reviewers reading AC3 believe no size guard existed, when one did and merely used the wrong unit.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace AC3's 'new module' with amending `test_alarm_descriptions_fit_the_aws_limit`: change the measure from `len(rendered)` to `len(rendered.encode('utf-8'))`, rename/repurpose `_AWS_ALARM_DESCRIPTION_MAX` and the failure message from '1024-character' to '1024-BYTE', keep and possibly raise its existing `measured >= 18` floor, and confirm it FAILS pre-fix / PASSES post-fix (AC4). If a separate module is genuinely warranted, state the Rule-of-Three justification and how the two guards avoid drift.
